newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dasa MTU unit 97 sales seen rising 17 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dasa MTU unit 97 sales seen rising 17 pct.

text.p: The aircraft engine unit of Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG said on Monday that a surge civil avaiaton orders caused sales in the first five months of the year to rise 26 percent and orders to rise 50 percent.

For the full year, Motoren- und Turbinen-Union (MTU) expected sales to rise at a more moderate rate of 17 percent to 2.7 billion marks, with profit improving over last year's level, said MTU chief Rainer Hertrich at the Paris airshow.
MTU did not provide precise figures for the first five months of 1997.
"It is primarily the civil business that has been driving growth so far this," he said at a news conference. "We do not expect to hold this level for the whole year."
Civil aviation makes up 65 percent of MTU's sales, with the rest coming from engines for military planes.
Dasa, a unit of car maker Daimler-Benz AG, said on Sunday that first-quarter sales rose 39 percent to 3.9 billion marks, and forecasted 1997 sales would rise eight percent to 14 billion marks.
Dasa also predicted further improvement in profit in 1997. Last year it had an operating profit of five million marks on sales of 13.1 billion marks.
